{{Short description|American physicist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2020}}
'''James C. Garland''' is a [[physicist]], author and professor, and formerly the 20th president of [[Miami University]] in [[Oxford, Ohio]].

Garland was educated at [[Princeton University]] (BA) and [[Cornell University|Cornell Univ.]] (PhD), in the field of [[condensed matter physics]], and was an N.S.F [[Postdoctoral Fellow]] at the [[:University of Cambridge]]. He has written more than 100 research papers,<ref>[https://journals.aps.org/pr/abstract/10.1103/PhysRev.185.1009 ''Low-Field Hall Coefficient of Indium'' Cornell University research paper], retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> and is the author of ''Saving Alma Mater: A Rescue Plan for America's Public Universities'',<ref>[https://www.press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/S/bo6963834.html ''Saving Alma Mater: A Rescue Plan for America's Public Universities'']: Univ. of Chicago Press (2009), retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> in which he advances changes in public university funding. He is now a Miami University [[president emeritus]]. Garland is a lifelong amateur radio operator, with the FCC call letters W8ZR ([https://www.w8zr.net www.w8zr.net])

==Ohio State University==

From 1970 to 1996 Garland taught at [[Ohio State University]]<!--Wikipedians do not use "The" as part of Ohio State's name; it is considered a marketing gimmick, and routinely deleted.--> as a physics professor. He became Ohio State's graduate and research studies acting vice president, materials research laboratory director, department of physics chairperson, dean of the college of mathematical and physical sciences, and its dean of arts and sciences.

In 1991, Garland wrote a widely disseminated article on the art of presenting research at scientific conferences.<ref>[https://cires.colorado.edu/jimenez/AtmChem/Advice_Beginning_Speakers.pdf ''Advice to Beginning Physics Speakers''] (1991), retrieved 16 March 2011</ref>

==Miami University, Oxford, OH==

Garland became the President of Miami University in 1996. In 2002, his stated aim was to make Miami the "First in 2009",<ref>[http://www.miamihockeycamps.com/goggin-ice-center.cfm Miami University Hockey Camps] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101215004401/http://www.miamihockeycamps.com/goggin-ice-center.cfm |date=15 December 2010 }}, retrieved 16 March 2011</ref> the university's bicentennial year. To achieve this status, he developed a strategy to raise intellectual quality and apply [[Quantitative property|quantitative]] [[benchmarking]] and [[best practice]], and led Miami in a significant [[Capital Improvement Plan|capital improvement]] and construction program. [[Financial endowment|Endowment]]s doubled, and student applications increased by sixty percent.{{citation needed|date=March 2011}}

He equalized in-state and out-of-state tuition fees and provided scholarships for Ohio students based on need.<ref>[http://www.miami.muohio.edu/news/article/view/3138 News Release: "New Tuition Plan"]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, Miami University (2003) retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> In 2004, Miami became the first Ohio [[public university]] to offer students [[domestic partner]] benefits, while Garland publicly criticized the [[Ohio State Issue 1 (2004)|Ohio Issue 1]] amendment to the State Constitution that defined the status of non-marriage relationships.{{citation needed|date=March 2011}}

In 1999, Garland recommended to the Miami's [[board of trustees]] that four men's sports should cease to be supported to fulfill the university's legal obligation under [[Title IX]]; due to financial constraint he thought it difficult to meet [[gender equity]] without such cuts.<ref>[http://www.miami.muohio.edu/news/article/view/2521 Miami University News Release 1999: ''Title IX May Cost Miami Four Men's Sports''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628183707/http://www.miami.muohio.edu/news/article/view/2521 |date=28 June 2011 }}, retrieved 16 March 2011</ref> A court [[Class action|action]] in the [[United States Court of Appeals]] was brought against Miami University in 2002 by Miami's sports clubs, claiming the cuts constituted [[gender discrimination]]; the action failed.<ref>[https://caselaw.findlaw.com/us-6th-circuit/1161180.html United States Court of Appeals, Sixth Circuit: ''Miami University Wrestling Club v. Miami University''], retrieved 16 March 2011</ref>

Garland completed his tenure as Miami President in 2006.

==''Saving Alma Mater''==
In 2009, Garland expounded his views on the state of higher education in public universities in his book ''Saving Alma Mater: A Rescue Plan for America's Public Universities''. In an interview with ''Inside Higher Education'' in October 2009, where he presents public university education as vital but in need of change to survive successfully, he talks of four main areas of change that need to be addressed:

*He sees public universities becoming autonomous through deregulation, run by independent trustees who decide educational and financial policies.
*He argues that taxpayers' money should support less-well-off students through scholarships, not subsidize campuses; higher income students would pay more, lower income less. Best value schools would prosper and overall student numbers would rise. Research, low-enrollment, and vital programs would be protected.
*He sees university personnel cost as being the largest area of budget. Efficiency should be increased through voluntary financial incentives, and reducing committee sizes and numbers.
*He believes that candidate selection of senior administrators, presidents and chancellors by search committees and vested interests is inefficient and ineffective, and should operate more like private-sector universities.  He also argues that state governors who typically appoint trustees should be educated about how to select qualified and effective candidates.<ref>[http://www.insidehighered.com/news/2009/10/23/garland Inside Higher Education: ''Saving Alma Mater''], 23 October 2009, retrieved 15 March 2011</ref>

Garland's views were acknowledged in ''[[The New York Times]]''.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2010/01/03/education/edlife/03books-t.html Review: ''Saving Alma Mater''] ''The New York Times'', 29 December 2009, retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> He spoke on topics raised in ''Saving Alma Mater'' at the [[University of Cincinnati]],<ref>[http://www.uc.edu/news/NR.aspx?id=12936 ''Saving Alma Mater'': University of Cincinnati: speech by J.C. Garland.] 14 January 2011, retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> the University of Illinois, the University of Colorado, Wisconsin, and other venues. He spoke to the ''Pittsburgh Tribune-Review'' about financial concerns at [[Penn State University]],<ref>[http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/news/s_727389.html#ixzz1GgUTtVsP: "Not much fat in Penn State budget, national study shows"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110320042041/http://www.pittsburghlive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/news/s_727389.html#ixzz1GgUTtVsP: |date=20 March 2011 }} ''Pittsburgh Tribune-Review'', 15 March 2011, retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> He told of his criticism of what he saw as the mismanagement of campuses to ''[[The Washington Post]]'',<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121011093007/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/shortstack/2009/12/how_to_reinvigorate_public_uni.html "Saving Alma Mater'': ''How to reinvigorate public universities".  J. C. Garland blog]. ''The Washington Post'', 15 December 2009, retrieved 15 March 2011</ref> and in 2005, before the book was published, he expressed some of the same ideas to the same newspaper.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/12/29/AR2005122901312.html "How to Put College Back Within Reach"], ''The Washington Post'' 30 December 2005, retrieved 15 March 2011</ref>
